label: SQL Style
summary: SQL formatting and query-construction conventions inside SSL strings.
must_follow: Use multiline SQL strings for non-trivial queries and put major clauses on separate lines.
Pre-compute complex values before interpolating them into SQLExecute placeholders.
Use PrepareArrayForIn or SQLExecute array expansion for dynamic IN clauses when appropriate; do not build an IN clause by hand when a safer array helper or parameter array is available.
Inside SQL strings, write SQL keywords and built-in functions in uppercase.

Preserve the author's casing for table names, column names and aliases; force-folding is dialect-conditional (safe on Oracle, but breaks case-sensitive SQL Server collations), so lowercase only Oracle-only code.
avoid: Do not mix named and positional placeholder mental models in the same call.
Do not put a trailing semicolon inside an embedded SQL string — "SELECT ... ;" is not the convention; end the SSL statement, not the SQL text.

elements.name: SQLExecute
elements.summary: Executes SQL and returns either query results or a success flag.

elements.name: RunSQL
elements.summary: Executes a non-query SQL statement and returns .T. on success. Under default settings, a failed statement raises an error.

elements.name: LSearch
elements.summary: Returns a single value from a SQL query, or a caller-supplied fallback when the query produces no scalar result.

elements.name: LSelect1
elements.summary: Executes a parameterized SQL SELECT command and returns the result as an array of rows.

elements.name: GetDataSet
elements.summary: Executes a SQL query on the default database connection and returns the result as an XML dataset string.

elements.name: BuildStringForIn
elements.summary: Builds a quoted string list for a SQL IN clause from an array.

elements.name: PrepareArrayForIn
elements.summary: Prepares an array for SQL IN clause helpers by mutating it in place.
